name: Canyons to the Coast — January 2027
subtitle: Valley of Fire · Zion · Page · Monument Valley · Grand Canyon · Los Angeles · Death Valley
summary: Out of Las Vegas through Zion, Page, Monument Valley and the Grand Canyon while it is coldest, then west to Los Angeles and down into Death Valley so the trip ends warm. The motorhome never sleeps on the canyon rim — the Grand Canyon night is at Cameron, and after the canyon day you drive on to Kingman, about 2,500 feet lower. This is the working draft; costs on this page are still from the earlier version of the route.
startEnd: Las Vegas, NV (Harry Reid International — LAS)

mustSee.name: Fire Wave
mustSee.why: Striped red and white sandstone at the end of a short flat walk. Valley of Fire in a single stop.

mustSee.name: Zion Canyon Scenic Drive
mustSee.why: In January the shuttle stops running and you drive the canyon yourself — a road closed to private cars most of the year.

mustSee.name: Horseshoe Bend
mustSee.why: $10 for the whole vehicle and a 1.5-mile walk. Does what a $580 Antelope Canyon tour does, for a sixtieth of the price.

mustSee.name: The Mittens at sunrise
mustSee.why: If you splurge once on this trip, splurge on a room that faces these.

mustSee.name: Desert View Watchtower
mustSee.why: Coming in from the east means this is your first sight of the Grand Canyon. It is the best one there is.

mustSee.name: Mather Point
mustSee.why: The classic view straight across the canyon, on your one full day there — snow on the rim over red rock, and the park as empty as it gets all year.

mustSee.name: Badwater Basin
mustSee.why: The lowest point in North America, 282 ft below sea level. Walk out onto the salt flats.

mustSee.name: Mesquite Flat Dunes
mustSee.why: Go at sunrise. Dunes the kids can run down, before the wind picks up and the light goes flat.

mustSee.name: Zabriskie Point
mustSee.why: Golden badlands at sunset, ten minutes from where you sleep. The best view in Death Valley for the least effort.

watchOuts.title: Book these first
watchOuts.text: Goulding's at Monument Valley, the RV park at Cameron, then Zion. After those: a Valley of Fire site for night 1 (you arrive in the dark), an RV park in Los Angeles, and a Las Vegas RV park for night 13.

watchOuts.title: Five cold nights, all between −1 and −4°C
watchOuts.text: NOAA January average lows: Zion about −1°C, Page −3°C, Goulding’s −4°C, Cameron about −4°C. The rim, at −7°C, is avoided on purpose. Run the propane furnace, not the heat pump, which stops working around 4°C. Disconnect the city water hose at night and run off the fresh tank. A cold snap can put any stop 5–10°C below its average, so check the forecast before the cold stretch.

watchOuts.title: Freeze damage is charged to you
watchOuts.text: Rental companies push freeze damage onto the renter and treat a burst pipe as negligent damage at full repair cost. Confirm in writing that the unit is not winterized, that the water system is live, and that they have noted your cold-weather destinations on the booking.

watchOuts.title: Death Valley is still closing roads
watchOuts.text: Flood damage persists. Bonnie Clare Road and Scotty's Castle are closed with no reopening date, North Highway has loose gravel and missing shoulders, southern Badwater Road has soft shoulders and unpaved sections, and Emigrant Campground is closed indefinitely. Check the park's conditions page a week before departure.

watchOuts.title: Fill up before you drive in
watchOuts.text: Fill up in Nevada, Utah and Arizona. Top off before entering Death Valley, where in-park fuel at Furnace Creek is notably expensive.

watchOuts.title: The park pass does not cover everything
watchOuts.text: The America the Beautiful pass covers Death Valley, Zion, the Grand Canyon and Glen Canyon. It does not cover Monument Valley, which is a Navajo tribal park ($8 per person), or Valley of Fire, which is a Nevada state park.

watchOuts.title: Price the unlimited-miles package
watchOuts.text: If the rental charges per mile at around $0.35, 1,655 miles adds roughly $580. Always price the unlimited-miles package as an alternative.

watchOuts.title: Day 12 is the weather buffer
watchOuts.text: The second Death Valley day is deliberately free. If snow costs you a day in the cold first week, absorb it there.

pros: Monument Valley and the Grand Canyon, plus Zion, Death Valley and a taste of Los Angeles, out and back from one airport.
The cold comes first and is over by day 7. After that every night is warmer than the last, finishing in Death Valley.
The motorhome never sleeps on the Grand Canyon rim — Cameron is about 2,500 feet lower and about 3°C warmer.
Day 1 is only 52 miles, so the late RV pickup and the shopping fit.
Winter opens Zion Canyon Scenic Drive to private vehicles, unless the shuttle is running for the holiday.
January is the emptiest month of the year at the Grand Canyon.
A spare day in Death Valley at the end, warm, for weather or for doing nothing.
cons: Five nights around or below freezing in the first week, between −1 and −4°C on average.
Two long days: Kingman to Los Angeles is 337 miles, and Los Angeles to Death Valley 275.
Day 7 ends with about 175 miles after dark, out of the Grand Canyon to Kingman — partly on high road that can ice over at night.
One night at Monument Valley and one full day at the Grand Canyon — enough to see them, not to linger.
Parking a motorhome in Los Angeles is awkward; plan on one RV park and getting around from there.
Death Valley still has flood damage: Scotty's Castle and Bonnie Clare Road are closed indefinitely.

notConsidered.reason: Strong park, but it sits on the opposite side of the map from Monument Valley. Cannot have both in two weeks.
The warmest and most kid-friendly stop available, but on the western route only.
No hookups, no potable water, no cell service, and the York Fire burned close to 100,000 acres in 2023 including much of the Cima Dome Joshua tree forest.
In January the lake is too cold to swim, which removes the main reason to go. London Bridge is a ten-minute stop.

notConsidered.place: Saguaro NP and Lost Dutchman SP
notConsidered.reason: Both good, but adding them means a 400-mile I-10 leg — the worst driving day in any version of this trip.
Sits at 8,000 feet. Genuinely miserable in January.
Trailer rentals do not include a tow vehicle, and the major rental companies prohibit towing outright. Turo treats towing as a prohibited use that voids damage protection.

moneySavers.detail: Lower Antelope now costs $80.50 per person plus a $15 Navajo permit — about $580 for six. Upper runs $115-140 per person. The famous light beams only appear between 11am and 1pm from March to October, so in January you would pay peak-adjacent prices for a canyon without its main feature.
A 1.5-mile round-trip walk, no tour, no permit. $10 total for the whole group.
A genuine slot canyon you walk yourself on BLM land, about 90 minutes from Page toward Kanab. The access road is dirt and turns to slop when wet.

moneySavers.item: Sleep in Beatty, not in the park
moneySavers.detail: The largest single lever in the car-and-hotels build.
Buy bedding and kitchen gear at a Las Vegas store on day one for $200-300 and leave it behind. Cheaper than per-person kit fees for six.
Covers Death Valley, Zion, Grand Canyon and Glen Canyon. It does NOT cover Monument Valley, which is a Navajo tribal park, or Valley of Fire, which is a Nevada state park.

options.name: Motorhome
options.summary: Transport and lodging in one vehicle, so there is nothing to book at six separate stops and you cook instead of eating out — but seven nights below freezing, and three places on this route it simply cannot go.

vehicle.detail: Cruise America C30 · sleeps 7 · 7 seatbelts · 30 ft long, 8.33 ft wide, 12.2 ft high
vehicle.notes: Book by seatbelt count, not sleeping capacity. The smaller C25 measures 24.93 ft long, 8.33 ft wide and 12.20 ft high — it clears Death Valley's 25-foot roads but is still too wide and too tall for Zion's Mount Carmel Highway.

1.label: Pickup from 1pm.
1.text: Leave the shopping list ready so you can be out of Las Vegas by about 3:30.

4.label: This is why it is 160 miles.
4.text: The Zion–Mount Carmel tunnel is closed to vehicles your size, so the day goes round via Hurricane, Colorado City and Kanab. The map shows the long way.

5.label: Not in the motorhome:
5.text: The Navajo Nation bars RVs from the 17-mile loop by category, not by size. What you can still do for free: the visitor center overlook and the 3.2-mile Wildcat Trail. A Navajo-guided 4x4 tour runs $70–95 each.

11.label: Not in the motorhome:
11.text: Artist's Drive and the final climb to Dante's View are closed to vehicles over 25 feet.

13.label: Get it ready tonight.
13.text: Dump the tanks, clean and pack this afternoon so the morning return is quick.

14.label: Back by 11am.
14.text: Then a hotel for the last night.

options.name: Car and lodging
options.tagline: More expensive, warmer, and unlocks three places the RV can't reach
options.summary: A seven-seater and a room every night. It costs meaningfully more, and almost all of the gap is food and lodging — but nobody sleeps below freezing, and it opens up three places on this route the motorhome is barred from.

costs.notes: Two versions of the same trip. "Best value" sleeps in Beatty rather than inside Death Valley, which alone saves close to $1,000 over three nights — the single biggest lever in the whole budget. "Best location" puts you inside the parks and at The View in Monument Valley.

to.name: Valley of Fire State Park, NV

days.headline: Collect the RV, shop, and out by dusk
days.notes: The motorhome is ready no earlier than 1pm. Shop for bedding, kitchen kit and groceries in Las Vegas, leave by about 3:30, and you reach Valley of Fire around dark. You will not see much tonight — the park is tomorrow morning. Book the campsite ahead rather than hunting for one in the dark. January lows here average 4.5°C.

from.name: Valley of Fire State Park, NV

days.headline: Valley of Fire at sunrise, then Zion
days.notes: Wake up inside the park: the Fire Wave, Atlatl Rock and White Domes in the morning, then leave around 12:30–1pm to reach Zion before dark. Springdale averages a January low of about −1°C — the mildest of the cold nights.

days.notes: In winter you can usually drive the Zion Canyon Scenic Drive yourself — check whether the shuttle is running over the holiday weekend, because then the road closes to cars. Shaded trails like Emerald Pools ice over in the mornings; go late and bring traction spikes. The Narrows is out in January.

days.headline: Sunrise at the Mittens, then the canyon from the east
days.notes: Sunrise over the Mittens and the Wildcat Trail, then west to Cameron. In the afternoon, drive 30 miles in to Desert View Watchtower for your first look at the Grand Canyon, and back to Cameron for the night. You do not sleep on the rim: Grand Canyon Village averages −7°C in January, Cameron about −4°C.

days.headline: A full day at the Grand Canyon, then Kingman after dark
days.notes: Leave Cameron in the morning and come in by the east entrance: Desert View, the rim road west, Yavapai and Mather Point, the top of Bright Angel. Stay for sunset, then drive out through Tusayan and Williams and west on I-40, arriving in Kingman around 9pm — with late food in town and a January low of about −1°C instead of Cameron’s −4°C. Take the stretch down to Williams slowly: around 7,000 ft it can ice over after dark. Seligman is on this road, but you pass it at night.

days.headline: The long drive to the coast
days.notes: One of the two long days, 337 miles. The Powerhouse museum on Route 66 in Kingman before you go, then across the Mojave on I-40 and I-15 and down into Los Angeles. Santa Monica averages a January low of about 10°C.

days.headline: A full day in Los Angeles
days.notes: Park the motorhome at one RV park with hookups and get around from there — parking an RV in the city is the hard part. Monday 18 January is the MLK holiday, so expect crowds anywhere popular.

days.headline: Out of LA and down into Death Valley
days.notes: The other long day, 275 miles, over Towne Pass on the way in. North through the Mojave and down to Furnace Creek, 190 feet below sea level. January lows average about 6°C — the warmest nights of the trip.

days.notes: Zabriskie Point at sunrise, then 122 miles to an RV park in Las Vegas. Dump the tanks, clean, and pack in the afternoon so the return in the morning is easy.
